summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. She studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, the University of Bonn, the Manjushree Centre of Tibetan Culture, and the University of Marburg, and held posts at Vienna and Marburg.

Adelheid Mette (1934–2023) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg. She taught Ruixuan Chen and served as professor at the University of Munich and chair of Indology at the University of Münster.

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, Harvard University, and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She held faculty positions at the University of Chicago and the University of Basel.
Adeu Rinpoche (1931–2007) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche, and later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère (1853–1917) was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He founded Le Prolétaire, Typographie Française, and the Société ethnologique de Paris, and served as Résident de France at Kratie in Cambodia.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye (1906–1975) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He taught at Rajaram College, Shivaji University, and was founding professor of the Jaina Chair at the University of Mysore.

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (1807–1887) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Franz Bopp, A. W. von Schlegel, and others. He worked at the East India Company Library and Breslau University.

Adolf Holtzmann (1810–1870) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Munich, and Berlin under Othmar Frank, J. A. Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg.

Adolf Kaegi (1849–1923) was a Swiss Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as professor of Sanskrit and classical philology at the University of Zurich.

Adolf Kießling (1837–1893) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology who taught Wilhelm Schulze. He held posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), the University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and the University of Göttingen.

Adolf Kirchhoff (1826–1908) was a German linguist and historian. He studied under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh at the University of Berlin, where he later served as professor of classical philology alongside a post at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium.

Adolphe Regnier (1804–1884) was an Indologist, linguist, and historian who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France, the École Normale Supérieure, the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and the Palace of Fontainebleau.

Adrian Zenz is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He has held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Adrián Muñoz is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and as a lecturer of South Asian religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo and the University of Bonn, and held an affiliation with the University of Warsaw (attested 2008).
Agathe Keller is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She has held posts at REHSEIS (attested 2006), as well as CNRS and Paris Diderot University (both attested 2017).

Agathon Benary (1807–1860) was a German linguist. He earned his doctorate from Halle-Wittenberg, also studying at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp, and held teaching posts at the Köllnisches Gymnasium and the University of Berlin.

Agehananda Bharati (1923–1991) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna. He taught at Delhi, Banaras Hindu, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, Tokyo, and Kyoto, and became Ford-Maxwell Professor at Syracuse University.

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University, Toruń, and held affiliations with Cornell University (attested 2009) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev (1853–1938) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned his Geshey Lharampa degree at Drepung Monastery. He founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and Atsagat Datsan, and taught Ngawang Wangyal and the 13th Dalai Lama.
